q: 181. In an electrical drawings, a fuse is shown as .............
options: a small circle in the line
a slight zigzag on the line
an opening or break in the line
explain: In standard electrical/circuit symbol conventions, a fuse is represented as a break or opening in the line (often with a small rectangle), symbolizing the circuit element that opens under fault conditions.

q: 182. Free hand sketching can be done only when one has .............
explain: Good freehand sketching requires a combination of skill/proficiency, regular practice, and patience together, making 'all of these' the correct comprehensive answer.

q: 183. The angle that isometric lines make with each other is .............
explain: The isometric lines (edges parallel to the isometric axes) are mutually inclined at 120° to each other, giving the standard isometric drawing its symmetric triangular appearance.

q: 184. A square in a regular multi-view projection appears in an isometric view as .............
explain: A square face, when drawn in isometric view (inclined to the viewer along isometric axes), is foreshortened into a rhombus shape.

q: 185. The illusion of depth in paintings is depicting by .............
explain: Aerial (atmospheric) perspective creates the illusion of depth in paintings through variations in color, tone, and clarity (distant objects appearing hazier/lighter), as distinct from linear (vanishing-point) perspective methods.

q: 186. The number of stages that are necessary to get the orthographic views of a solid having its axis inclined to both the reference planes .............
explain: When a solid's axis is inclined to both HP and VP, obtaining its true orthographic views requires a sequence of three stages: drawing it in simple position, tilting the axis to the given inclination with one plane, then further changing position relative to the other plane.

q: 187. A tetrahedron is resting on its face on the HP with a side perpendicular to the VP. Its front view will be .............
explain: With a tetrahedron resting on a triangular face on HP and one edge perpendicular to VP, the front view (projected along the direction perpendicular to VP) appears as an isosceles triangle due to the way the base edge foreshortens.

q: 188. A square pyramid is resting on a face in the VP. The number of dotted lines that will appear in the front view .............
explain: With the square pyramid resting on a triangular face against VP, the hidden (invisible) edges behind the visible face project as two dotted (hidden) lines in the front view.

q: 189. Minimum distance between blackboard and first row of benches should not be less than ............. in school building.
explain: School design norms specify a minimum distance of 4 m between the blackboard and the first row of benches, ensuring students in front do not strain their eyes or necks.

q: 190. Minimum plinth level for school building is ............. above the road level.
explain: Building norms for school buildings require the plinth to be raised a minimum of 400 mm above the road level, protecting the structure from surface water and dampness.

q: 191. The method by which the development of surface of an oblique solid is obtained .............
explain: Since an oblique solid's surface lacks the regular symmetry needed for exact radial-line or parallel-line development, its development is obtained approximately, using the approximation method.

q: 192. Methods for the development of solids are .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'triangular method' is marked as the sole correct answer, though in general practice, parallel-line, radial-line, and triangulation methods are all standard techniques for surface development of solids.

q: 193. Scale usually used in civil engineering drawing are .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'enlarged scale' is marked correct; in practice civil engineering drawings (site plans, layouts) most commonly use reduced scales since buildings/structures are much larger than the drawing sheet, but the given key selects option (a).

q: 194. Diagonal scales are used for measurement of .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'two unit' is marked correct here; conventionally, diagonal scales are valued specifically for reading three successive units (e.g., meters, decimeters, centimeters), but the given key selects option (b) for this item.

q: 195. Free hand sketch is normally used for .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'final' is marked correct; conventionally freehand sketches are used for quick concept development and discussion rather than as final deliverables, but the given key selects option (b).

q: 196. Isometric drawing fall into a larger category of drawings known as .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'perspective drawings' is marked correct; conventionally isometric drawings fall under the broader category of pictorial (or axonometric) drawings rather than perspective drawings, but the given key selects option (d).

q: 197. If a thin rectangular plate of 60 mm × 30 mm is inclined at an angle of 60° to HP its top view may be .............
explain: When the 60 mm side (perpendicular to VP) is inclined at 60° to HP, its projected length in the top view foreshortens to approximately 30 mm (60×cos60°=30), making the top view a square of 30 mm side (30×30).

q: 198. In multi-view orthographic projection, the front view of a circular plane may be .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'an ellipse' is marked correct here; conventionally, depending on the plane's orientation, the front view of a circular plane can be a circle, ellipse, or straight line, so 'any one of these' would be the general case, but the given key selects option (b) for this specific item.

q: 199. If both front and top views of a plane are straight lines the true shape will lie on .............
explain: When both principal views collapse to straight lines, the plane is perpendicular to both HP and VP, meaning it is parallel to the profile plane; conventionally this would place the true shape on the profile plane specifically, but per this reference, option (d) is marked as the general answer.

q: 200. If a circular plane is inclined at 30° with the HP and 60° with the VP its side view will be .............
explain: Since the given inclinations (30° to HP and 60° to VP) sum to 90°, the plane is perpendicular to the profile plane, so its side view is seen edge-on as a straight line.

q: 201. For drawing thin lines of uniform thickness the pencil should be sharpened in the form of .............
explain: A chisel-edge sharpened pencil maintains a consistent line width over long strokes, making it ideal for drawing thin lines of uniform thickness, especially with straightedges.

q: 202. Most prevailing size of drawing sheets used in preparation of municipal drawing for building permit is .............
explain: Municipal building permit drawings are commonly prepared and submitted on A1 size sheets, balancing detail and manageable size for official records.

q: 203. Axonometric projection is a special type of .............
explain: Axonometric projection (including isometric, dimetric, trimetric) is a subtype of orthographic projection, using parallel projectors perpendicular to the plane but with the object rotated to show multiple faces.

q: 204. Which of the following scale is used for converting miles into kilometers .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'diagonal scale' is marked correct; conventionally a comparative scale is specifically designed to relate two different units (like miles and kilometers) on one scale, but the given key selects option (a) for this item.

q: 205. If a point moves in a plane in such a way that the sum of its distances from two fixed points is constant the curve so traced is called .............
explain: This is the classical definition of an ellipse: the locus of points whose sum of distances from two fixed points (the foci) remains constant.

q: 206. Name the curve traced out by a point moving in a place such that the difference between its distances from two fixed points is constant .............
explain: By definition, a hyperbola is the locus of points where the difference (not sum) of distances from two fixed foci remains constant.

q: 207. Dimension lines and projection lines are shown as .............
options: continuous thin lines with zig zag
explain: As per standard line conventions, both dimension lines and projection (extension) lines are drawn as continuous thin lines.
A graphos is a type of pen with an interchangeable metal nib used for both drawing and lettering (writing) on technical drawings, making it a drawing-and-writing instrument.

q: 209. Oblique projections are of .............
explain: Oblique projections (cavalier and cabinet types) commonly use receding lines drawn at either 30° or 45° to the horizontal, so both angles are used depending on the projection type.

q: 210. The ratio of length of drawing to the actual length of the object is called .............
explain: This ratio, drawing length to actual length (expressed in the same units), is precisely the definition of the Representative Fraction (R.F.).

q: 211. The length to height ratio of a closed filled arrow head is .............
explain: As per drawing standards, an arrowhead used on dimension/leader lines is drawn with a length-to-height (width) ratio of approximately 3:1, giving it a narrow, pointed appearance.

q: 212. The two recommended systems of placing the dimensions are .............
explain: The two standard, recommended methods for orienting and reading dimension figures on a drawing are the aligned system and the unidirectional system.

q: 213. Which of the following is the correct statement for dimensioning a view?
options: All of them should be placed within a view
All of them should be placed close to the parts being dimensioned
They should be marked from visible outlines rather than from hidden line
Dimensions indicated in one view may be repeated in another view
explain: Good dimensioning practice requires dimensions to be taken/marked from visible outlines rather than from hidden (dashed) lines, since hidden-line dimensions are less reliable and clear.

q: 214. Development of sphere is done by .............
options: parallel line or radial line method
explain: Since a sphere's doubly curved surface cannot be developed exactly, it is approximately developed using the zone (band) method or the lune (gore) method, both specialized techniques for spherical surfaces.

q: 215. The most suitable tool to draw freehand is .............
explain: An HB pencil, with its medium hardness/softness, provides good control and visibility for general freehand sketching, making it the most suitable common tool among the options.

q: 216. There should be provision of 1 toilets per ............. students in school buildings.
explain: School sanitation norms in this reference specify one toilet should be provided for every 15 students.

q: 217. The dimension lines are marked in a building drawing with .............
explain: In building drawings, dimension line terminators are conventionally shown using either arrowheads or oblique ticks (short diagonal strokes), so 'arrows or ticks' is correct.

q: 218. The ISO A0 size of drawing is defined as having an area of .............
explain: The ISO A0 sheet size is defined such that its area equals exactly 1 square meter, from which all other A-series sizes are derived by successive halving.

q: 219. The line connecting a view to note is called .............
explain: A leader line is a thin line (often ending in an arrowhead or dot) used to connect a note, label, or dimension to the specific feature it refers to on the drawing.

q: 220. T square is used to draw .............
explain: The T-square's blade slides along the board's working edge, making it primarily suited for drawing horizontal lines (vertical and inclined lines require set squares used in conjunction with it).

q: 221. The equipment used to draft vertical and angular line is .............
explain: Vertical and angular (inclined) lines are drawn using a set square placed against the T-square's blade, combining both tools together.

q: 222. Vernier scales are used to read .............
explain: A vernier scale is designed to allow precise reading of very small fractional units/subdivisions beyond the smallest main scale division, increasing measurement accuracy.

q: 223. In case of perspective projection, picture plane is placed .............
explain: In perspective projection, the picture plane is positioned between the observer's eye (station point) and the object, onto which the perspective view is projected.

q: 224. Free hand sketching can be done only when one has .............
explain: As with the earlier repeated item, effective freehand sketching requires a combination of patience and good practice together, supporting the 'all of the above' answer.

q: 225. The artificial light on the drawing board should be diffused light from .............
explain: Artificial lighting for a (typically right-handed) drafter should be diffused and directed from the left, avoiding shadows cast by the drafting hand and instruments over the work area.

q: 226. The isometric length of the edge of a cube is .............
explain: Since isometric projection uses the reduced isometric scale (~0.816 of true length), the isometric length of any edge, including a cube's, is less than its actual (true) length.

q: 227. When a bullet is shot in air the path traversed by the bullet is called .............
explain: Under gravity and ignoring air resistance, a projectile such as a bullet follows a parabolic trajectory through the air.

q: 228. Isometric drawings fall into the category of .............
explain: Isometric drawing is one specific type within the broader category of axonometric drawings, which are orthographic projections with the object rotated to reveal multiple faces.

q: 229. The projectors in isometric view are .............
explain: Isometric projection is a form of orthographic (parallel) projection, so its projectors remain parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 230. The scale used for drawing working details of element is .............
explain: Detailed working drawings of individual structural/building elements are typically drawn at a larger scale such as 1:25, providing sufficient clarity for construction-level detail.

q: 231. Conceptual layout plan developed for preliminary discussion is .............
explain: A line plan is a preliminary, simplified layout drawing (showing basic room arrangement as lines) prepared for initial concept discussion before detailed design work begins.

q: 232. In engineering drawing, auxiliary views are used to show details of .............
explain: Auxiliary views are specifically constructed to show the true shape and size of inclined (or oblique) surfaces, which appear foreshortened in the standard principal views.

q: 233. Isometric projection is .............
options: an orthographic projection of pictorial type
explain: Isometric projection is classified as a pictorial type of orthographic projection, since its parallel projectors remain perpendicular to the plane of projection while the object itself is tilted to reveal multiple faces.

q: 234. ............. maximum tangents can be drawn from an outside point on a circle.
explain: From any point located outside a circle, exactly two distinct tangent lines can be drawn to the circle, touching it at two separate points.

q: 235. The way of illustrating three dimensional objects in a two dimensional drawing is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'perspective' is marked correct here; more broadly, several methods (axonometric, perspective, oblique) are used to represent 3D objects in 2D, but the given key highlights perspective as the intended answer for this item.

q: 236. When primarily information is drawn in elevation, the interpretation is done by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'cavalier projection' is marked correct; cavalier oblique projection retains true (full) scale along the receding axis, which supports interpretation when the front (elevation) face carries the primary information.

q: 237. Which type of line has precedence over all other types of lines?
explain: Per line-precedence conventions in drafting, a visible (continuous, outline) line always takes precedence over hidden lines and center lines when they coincide on a drawing.

q: 238. The most suitable angle for the cone of vision for drawing perspective is .............
explain: For a natural, undistorted perspective view, the recommended cone of vision (viewing angle) is approximately 30°, beyond which noticeable distortion occurs near the edges.

q: 239. As built drawings are prepared by .............
explain: As-built drawings, documenting the actual completed construction (including field changes), are typically prepared by the contractor who executed the work.

q: 240. The paper size of A4 is .............
explain: The standard ISO A4 paper size is 210 mm × 297 mm, the most commonly used sheet size for general documents and smaller drawings.
